newsitem.title: USA: NY physical coffee - futures, differentials climb.
newsitem.headline: NY physical coffee - futures, differentials climb.

text.p: Roasters stayed sidelined on the New York physical coffee market this week, as CSCE futures prices continued to run higher, traders said.
"Roasters are just buying on a fill-in type basis," one trader said. "They are just waiting for speculators to bail out of the futures market."
To make matters worse for roasters, dealers said already hefty differentials also climbed this week.
Although Colombian dockworkers returned to work a week ago following a nine-day strike, traders said coffee exports have been slow getting back normal.
"The bottom line in Colombia is that they are still moving sporadically," one coffee broker said. "There is major backlog and it takes awhile to clean up."
Colombian MAMs for spot delivery netted 28-29 cents over "C" this week compared with 23-27 cents a week ago.
Differentials for mild coffees from El Salvador and Guatemala also rose this week, each fetching seven cents over the March contract, up one cent from last week.
While no U.S. roaster has raised its retail coffee prices yet, traders said increases may not be far off if the futures market stays near current levels.

"Roasters have got to be thinking about a price increase," one trader said. "Traditionally, they hate to raise prices in a market that is moving up. If it cools off and pulls back some then they will raise prices."
CSCE March coffee fell 0.90 cents a lb Friday to settle at 139.40. March ended 0.45 higher at 134.95.
